articles.title: Gold pares gains as Fed hike risks linger, eyes first weekly rise in three weeks
articles.desc: Gold prices saw a notable uptick as investors seized the opportunity for bargain purchases, despite a robust US dollar and escalating yields causing some hesitance. After reaching a 15-month low recently, spot gold has recorded a potential weekly increase of nearly 3%. Analysts caution, however, that ongoing rate increases from the Fed could stifle any further upward movement.

articles.title: Dollar set for weekly gain as risk appetite returns
articles.desc: The Australian dollar and other risk-sensitive currencies strengthened on Friday, buoyed by a positive shift in market sentiment. The US dollar also noted slight gains for the week amid ongoing volatility in equity markets. Anticipation surrounding future Federal Reserve rate hikes has influenced currency dynamics, while the dollar climbed against the Japanese yen amidst worries over intervention and rising inflation in Tokyo.

articles.title: European shares log strong weekly gains; markets await Spanish election
articles.desc: Investors in Europe are feeling optimistic as the benchmark share index climbs to a one-week high, with the pan-European STOXX 600 index up 1% after earlier losses. All eyes are now on Spain's upcoming snap election, which could reshape political landscapes in the region. The outcome may not only impact Spain but also ripple into crucial elections in France and Italy.

articles.desc: India's unincorporated MSME sector is witnessing faster productivity growth and narrowing regional disparities, with manufacturing recording the biggest gains, according to four rounds of ASUSE data. However, technology constraints, credit shortages, inadequate industrial workspaces and skill gaps continue to limit growth, calling for targeted policy interventions to help smaller businesses scale up.

articles.title: OPEC+ set to keep oil production targets steady: Report
articles.desc: OPEC+ is expected to maintain its production targets for Q1 2027, despite complexities arising from conflicting member production estimates and the ongoing Iran conflict. As the group reassesses its capacity data, some members voice their concerns over the initial findings. Analysts foresee a potential global oil surplus next year, increasing pressure on OPEC+, further complicated by recent exits of nations like the United Arab Emirates and Angola, indicating internal frictions.

articles.title: Copper sweeps higher as China offers stock market support
articles.desc: Copper prices experienced a notable increase after China's cabinet announced its support for the stock market, which positively impacted global equities. This rise follows a significant drop in copper prices earlier this month. Moreover, China's industrial profits recorded their highest growth in five months during October. The Yangshan premium for copper reflects a robust demand for imports, even in the face of recent downturns.

articles.title: Blackstone sells 1.55% stake in IGI for Rs 280 crore to meet public shareholding norms
articles.desc: Blackstone completed the sale of a 1.5 percent stake in International Gemological Institute through block deals. The transaction involved selling over 67.16 lakh shares at an average of Rs 417 each. As a result, Blackstone's holding decreased from 76.55 percent to 75 percent. The stake sale was necessary to comply with minimum public shareholding requirements under Sebi regulations. Following the sale, shares of International Gemological Institute rose by 1.

articles.desc: Eurozone government bond yields edged higher as investors shifted back towards riskier assets and oil prices rebounded amid escalating Middle East tensions. Markets also assessed the European Central Bank's policy outlook, with money markets pricing in two 25-bps rate hikes by June 2027, despite expectations of a weekly decline in yields.

articles.title: Rupee rally takes a hit as AI trade revival dents shares, currency sees weekly dip
articles.desc: The Indian rupee has seen a downturn against the US dollar, driven by a drop in local stocks and a rise in oil prices. Interestingly, foreign investments in Indian equities have rebounded, reaching approximately $16 billion this month. With growing interest in AI markets, the rupee's stability could be at risk.

articles.title: IORA nations must enhance collaboration: EAM Jaishankar
articles.desc: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar highlighted the significance of the Indian Ocean for global trade and energy security. He stated that regional cooperation is vital to address the shared challenges faced by littoral states. Jaishankar emphasized that IORA must adapt to geopolitical changes and enhance its collective voice. India's theme for IORA promotes innovation and resilience in the region.

articles.title: India bonds decline ahead of fresh debt sale as elevated oil prices fan inflation worries
articles.desc: Indian government bonds decreased in early trading due to rising oil prices and cautious investor sentiment. The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond yield increased significantly amid higher expectations for a rate hike. New Delhi is set to raise 330 billion rupees through a bond sale, contributing to market tension. Concerns over food-price pressures and inflation continue to influence the Reserve Bank of India's upcoming decision.

articles.title: Japan's JERA enters talks with Anthropic, Meta to build data centres
articles.desc: JERA, Japan's leading power generator, is actively engaging with prominent U.S. tech corporations to establish advanced data centers adjacent to its Tokyo-area plants. This initiative follows JERA's recent collaboration with Dell Technologies and RHAELM to boost AI infrastructure in Japan. A monumental $15 billion hyperscale data center is set for development in Chiba, attracting major players like Anthropic, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, and Google.

articles.title: Women express frustration, concern over Nvidia boss Jensen Huang's return
articles.desc: News of Jensen Huang's shocking return to Nvidia had barely landed when President Donald Trump posted an AI-generated image of the Nvidia cofounder holding up a red bra, surrounded by security personnel whisking him offstage, blood streaked across his face.  On November 17, board Chairman Harvey Jones said the company "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." Then President Donald Trump intervened.
